front.title: Accountable Principal References for Delegated Agent Requests: Properties and Evaluation

abstract.t: When a software agent makes a request on behalf of a person or an organization, the party that receives it often needs to know that someone answers for the request, without needing to know who. Several specifications in progress carry some reference to the principal behind an agent, and they make different choices about who learns the principal's identity, when the reference can be linked across services, who can resolve it, and how fast a withdrawn principal stops being accepted. This document states six properties of such a principal reference in testable terms, maps each to existing specifications that already provide part of it (OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange, the JWT profile for OAuth 2.0 access tokens, OAuth identity chaining, Token Status List and Selective Disclosure for JWTs), and gives a first-pass evaluation of five current drafts against them. It defines no token format, protocol or claim, and it does not rank the drafts.
